# Independent candidate code review 01

Decision: **reject**.

Reviewer: independent Codex subagent `/root/context_code_preflight`, invoked by the implementation agent outside Keepsail core under the active `codex-subagent-review/v1` recognition contract. Review completed at 2026-10-27 16:30 UTC (2026-10-28 Asia/Shanghai).

Exact object: `code:d2d165130aa6c4c779f955513f3c76760feb06cb1ec061b3f07718fb3e3034d1`, Change `2026-10-27-harness-knowledge-context`, commit `3206f70196114abb4cbf1e322c439f3742ff6b22`, branch `codex/harness-knowledge-context`, base `bb69097dffee4e782568da4ea688d06b5773cbf4`. The retained object is `integration-candidate-code-subject.json`, including its complete 33-file manifest and knowledge basis. This is a pre-acceptance candidate review, not final code authority, knowledge recognition, policy activation or real-host acceptance.

## Blocking findings

1. **[P2] Infer an existing opt-in only from an actual managed context hook.** `src/keepsail/adapters/agent/claude_code.py:217-219` searches all original settings bytes for the SessionStart command substring when `knowledge_context` is unspecified. A valid settings file containing only `permissions.allow: ["Bash(keepsail-hook --agent claude-code --event session-start *)"]`, and no hooks or previous opt-in, therefore causes ordinary `adapter install claude-code` to install the context PreToolUse/SessionStart/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit hooks. The isolated probe returned `/env/keepsail-hook --agent claude-code --context` as the default PreToolUse command. This unexpectedly activates the new entry/acquisition precondition and can deny product edits to users who did not opt in, contradicting H6 and the documented default-install contract. Parse the existing hooks structure and recognize only the intended managed context registration (or persist an explicit selected mode); unrelated permission strings must not select installation mode. Add a regression for this valid settings case. The same whole-file heuristic at line 299 should use the same structural mode test for uninstall.

2. **[P2] Recover outer approval/convention declarations in the replacement entry.** `src/keepsail/core/context.py:394-402` builds the declaration trace exclusively from native knowledge statements and directs the executor to `knowledge show` for the full trace. However, `src/keepsail/daemon/context_hook.py:256-289` accepts approval/convention/empty-set declarations with `project_context: true` and an empty `knowledge_versions` list, writes no native record for those declarations, and saves them only in the old entry's operation-log directory. Nothing loads these records into the current or replacement projection. In the isolated probe, session A explicitly recorded a project-context challenge with a reason and dependent path, then session B retrieved the current entry: the reason was absent, both projected and native statement lists were empty, and readiness returned true. This finding concerns the lost recorded unresolved declaration, not a demand that every self-report gain authority or globally block work. H1/H3/H4, plan line 168 and architecture C1/C6 require historical declarations and unresolved matters to remain visible across replacement while remaining distinct from current acquisition and recognized authority. Recover these records with their original Change/entry/manifest and decision/reason, including explicit pending/disposition status, without promoting them into native knowledge authority or treating an old declaration as this epoch's observation. Test a project-only challenge and an empty-set adoption through a new session/compact epoch.

## Review work and limits

I read the normative product architecture, the complete frozen adopted plan H1-H8, active recognition contract, source changes, settings merge/uninstall code, CLI/gate wiring, core projection and receipt validation, and the associated unit/process integration tests. The retained subject validates and its manifest is bound to the exact Git diff. The tracked tree and HEAD remained at the candidate during this review; unrelated untracked files were preserved. I did not modify repository source, policy, lifecycle records or ledger, and did not import evidence.

The main positive boundaries observed in code are explicit Change/session/entry binding; new-epoch invalidation; exact command/output matching; full page reconstruction before native per-version acquisition; CAS/idempotent delivery; frozen approval artifact and ratified-decision text; separate authority and telemetry digests; full supply checking before action-local knowledge checks; original lifecycle and lawful authoring allowances; and a selected edit surface whose context errors deny rather than become readiness. These observations are code review, not proof of host callbacks, semantic understanding or compliance.

The new reproductions are retained in `review-probe-01.py` and `review-probe-01-results.json`, with all temporary repositories/settings beneath the external `review-probe-01/` directory. They invoke the candidate code using isolated test fixtures and supplied callback objects. They are **not actual Claude host or cross-session acceptance**. The probe also confirms current strict rejection of a callback whose cwd is a valid workspace subdirectory; actual root/subdirectory host behavior remains an integration limitation to observe during H7, and is not an additional blocking finding here.

The implementation agent's full native verify was running independently; I do not claim its result. H7 actual user-operated Claude A/B development sessions and separately recognized v2/disposition are deliberately pending, and their absence is not the reason for this candidate rejection. A successful isolated process test cannot replace those stages. After fixes, review the new exact candidate; eventual real-development changes and final completion must retain the ordinary assessment/verify/done/exact review/import/attestation process. This retained candidate judgment must not be imported as final code approval while the Change is `IMPLEMENTATION_IN_PROGRESS`.
